chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever the snare (hibalah) catches from game, if it cuts off its hand or leg, leave it, for it is dead. And eat from what you catch while it is alive and you have mentioned the name of Allah over it.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali)
key_terms.اَلْحِبَالَةُ: The snare or net used for catching game
key_terms.مَيِّتٌ: Dead (implying natural death or death by injury, not ritual slaughter)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game caught in a snare if it dies by losing a limb?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between ritual slaughter (*dhabh*) and hunting (*sayd*) by establishing that if a snare kills the animal by severing a limb, it is considered *mayyitah* (not ritually slaughtered) and thus not permissible to eat unless the name of Allah was invoked at the moment of capture. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the timing of the *tasmiyah* (mentioning Allah's name) as a critical condition for the permissibility of game meat, distinguishing it from the general rules of slaughter.
